coverage.summary: General statewide antitrust rule, not specific to housing. It applies to any person, other than the end consumer of a product or service, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm. That includes residential rental owners regardless of building size, age or owner type. The statute sets no unit-count, construction-date or owner-type limits.

evidence.quoted_span: “Person” has the same meaning as defined in Section 16702 and does not include the end consumer of a product or service.

(a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

result.notes:
Changes to coverage:
- Removed other_conditions ('two or more persons and competitor data'). That text is part of the definition of the prohibited conduct, i.e. what counts as a common pricing algorithm. It does not limit which buildings, units or owners are covered, so it belongs in requirement, not coverage.
- Removed from the summary the claims about city bans in Berkeley, San Francisco and Santa Ana and San Diego's proposed ban. No document supports them.
- Removed the DX09 single-firm-algorithm note from the summary, because it describes conduct.
- Did not set may_preempt_local_rules. § 16729(c) only preserves 'antitrust laws', which (d)(1) defines as the provisions of this part; it says nothing about local rules.
- Set requires_unknown_facts to false. The rule reaches ordinary rental owners generally, and its trigger is landlord conduct, not a building class that assessor data cannot identify.
